text:
devon: Quick question — trying to let a service in a different tenant wrap/unwrap keys in our AKV via a guest principal. Getting 403 AuthorizationPermissionMismatch when calling /keys/<name>/wrap? Anyone seen this pattern with managed identities cross-tenant?

maria: cross-tenant + managed identity is usually a no-go. User-assigned MSIs are tenant-scoped, they don't become 'guests' in another tenant. For cross-tenant you need a service principal in the vault's tenant (app registration) or use a federated identity (workload identity). :warning:

maria: tl;dr options: 1) create an app registration in the vault tenant and give it RBAC crypto role; 2) use Workload Identity Federation (federated creds) so external oidc issuer can request tokens in the vault tenant; 3) if you control both tenants, invite a guest SP via B2B and grant roles (messy).

ash: ping on RBAC vs access policies — our AKV still uses access policies. Which is better for crypto ops (wrap/unwrap) in this case?

maria: prefer Azure RBAC for new setups. With RBAC you can assign the KeyVault Crypto roles directly to the app principal. Access policies are older and tie to the vault resource specifically. Note: if the vault has access policies enforced and you're assigning RBAC roles, you'll get confusions — check vault's "Azure role-based access control" setting.

ash: role name to assign?
maria: assign the least-privileged built-in role for key ops: "Key Vault Crypto User" (allows use of keys for wrap/unwrap/encrypt/decrypt). Use scope = the specific vault or key. Example CLI: ```bash
az role assignment create --assignee <app/client id> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>```

devon: thanks — token looks ok but tid claim is from other tenant. Is that the root cause?
maria: yes — token's tid must match the tenant where the service principal exists (the vault's AAD tenant) when using RBAC. If token is for the caller's tenant, AKV will reject. For cross-tenant flows either mint a token in the vault tenant (app registration there) or use federated credentials to get a token in that tenant without long-lived creds.

devon: what about envelope encryption and rotation? We're rewrapping DEKs after KEK rotation and want to avoid pulling plaintext. Best practice?
maria: do rewrap with wrapKey/unwrapKey where possible so plaintext DEK never leaves HSM. Pattern: 1) call UnwrapKey with old KEK to get DEK (in secure context) then WrapKey with new KEK — but that exposes DEK in process memory. Better: use Key Vault's rewrap pattern if supported: Encrypt(DEK) under old KEK then Decrypt with old KEK and Encrypt with new KEK inside AKV using key ops so customer data keys never leave service. If you can't avoid, rotate by issuing a new DEK and re-encrypt application data with the new DEK gradually (rolling re-encrypt).

ash: any logging/audit tips to help debug these 403s and tenant mismatches?

logbot: Diagnostic checklist: enable KeyVault diagnostic settings -> send to Log Analytics / Event Hub. Turn on AuditEvent category. Also enable Azure AD sign-in logs and conditional access logs for the service principal. Sample CLI to wire diagnostics: ```bash
az monitor diagnostic-settings create --name kv-diagnostics --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/<la-workspace> --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'```

devon: got it. I'll provision an app in the vault tenant with federated credentials and assign Key Vault Crypto User on the vault scope, enable diagnostics, and test wrap/unwrap. Will report back. :thumbsup:

maria: one more gotcha — if you're using Managed HSM vs Key Vault Keys, roles and APIs differ. Managed HSM uses soft-delete/no-access-policies and strictly RBAC. Confirm which service.

ash: noted. thanks team.
